_meta.method: WebSearch only (WebFetch blocked for trvlogue.com, nate.com, phtourguide.com, da.gov.ph in this session). Facts are from search-result snippets; null = not verified. No current (Nov 2026) exchange rate figures were found for any changer.
general_money_tips: Bring crisp, new-series USD 100 bills (Korean blogs: double exchange KRW->USD in Korea, USD->PHP in Boracay; one blog claims ~5-10% better than KRW->PHP directly -- unverified blog claim).
Check mid-market rate (e.g. on phone) before exchanging; compare posted boards at 2-3 changers (Wise guide).
Count pesos at the counter before leaving.
D'Mall changers are reported to pay better than beach-path changers but worse than big-city malls (phtourguide.com, undated).
Henann Garden Resort front desk also exchanges money (trvlogue 2026, convenient, likely lower rate).
KRW: forum reports say won can be changed in Boracay but at a poor rate (one post: 15%+ loss) -- old ESL Cafe forum posts, not verified for 2026.
ATM skimming devices were found on D'Mall ATMs in 2013 (Inquirer) -- prefer ATMs inside bank branches, shield PIN.

changers.name: Nikko Forex
changers.location: Station 2 / D'Mall area, a little off the main road down a side lane; sign is small and easy to miss. Of two previously known branches, one reported closed / moved.
changers.usd_rate_notes: trvlogue 2026 comparison (single traveler): best USD rate of all places compared, ahead of Golden Forex and D'Mall changers. No exact figure available.
changers.tips: Confirm which branch is operating before walking there; Korean blogger reported a wasted trip to a closed branch.
changers.korean_review: 한국 블로그에서 '환율 좋다고 유명한 곳'으로 가장 많이 언급. 두 지점 중 하나는 폐업/이전했다는 후기 있음.

changers.usd_rate_notes: trvlogue 2026: slightly better than D'Mall changers, below Nikko Forex. No figure.

price_benchmarks_non_boracay.mango: Metro Manila markets PHP 150-300/kg (DA, Dec 2024); Guimaras mango retail up to PHP 400/kg in premium markets incl. Boracay (Manila Bulletin, Jul 2026)
price_benchmarks_non_boracay.note: Boracay tourist prices likely higher than these (inference).

fruit_season.summary: Late November: mango is off-peak (peak Mar-Jun) but available year-round, possibly pricier. Lanzones commonly listed Aug-Dec, so likely still around. Mangosteen listed Jun/Aug-Nov by some sources, so tail end/uncertain. Rambutan peak Aug-Oct, so probably finished or scarce. Sources disagree.
fruit_season.mangosteen: Jun-Nov or Aug-Nov (sources vary); off-season production exists at higher prices

korea_quarantine.fresh_mango: PROHIBITED for travelers to carry in. Korea's Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency (농림축산검역본부) lists fresh fruits incl. mango as banned carry-on items. Philippine mango import is only allowed via designated commercial export orchards/packhouses, not personal luggage. Undeclared: fine up to KRW 10 million (reported for banned items). Must declare any agricultural item on arrival.
korea_quarantine.other_fresh_fruit: Also banned (mangosteen, rambutan etc. are fresh fruit).
korea_quarantine.dried_mango: Commercially processed, sealed dried mango (e.g. 7D) is widely bought by Korean travelers and a blog says it passes; however no official QIA statement was found. Hankyung (2025) quoting QIA: dried fruit containing seeds may be banned for some items. Dried mango slices have no seeds -- likely OK but declare if unsure.
korea_quarantine.recommendation: Eat fresh fruit in Boracay; bring only sealed commercial dried mango; if in doubt, declare at the plant quarantine desk on arrival (Incheon).
